chapter: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
title: The style of his first band and its influences
summary: Gil says ensemble playing was his style. He lists Ellington, Don Redman, McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Red Nichols and Casa Loma.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Speaking of style, I was going to ask you, I'm going to ask you just this one more question. How would you describe your style when you first started out, when you had your first band? Was there anything that was uniquely yours at that point that you would identify?

Ensemble I guess was really the style ................(VOICE FADES OUT). That would be things for everybody to play, you know, ensemble. Not just an ordinary ensemble but something with some (sincerity and spirit?) that we could all do together.
Right. Were you showing much influence of Louis Armstrong at that time?
I was influenced by Duke Ellington and oh, there were so many other orchestras that are all forgotten now. (Don Redman. NY.
Red Nichols and his Five Pennies

He had most of the good white players Red Nichols did. There were few very talented white players. White in quotes because people like Jack Teagarden. If you ever saw Jack Teagarden you'd know he was part African too. He was never considered that. He was very talented.
I used to hear the bands come from New York when I was a kid you know in highschool. I was tuned in on the Casa Loma Orchestra.
Oh, (Glen Gray Graves?). Yes, yes, yes.

Before anybody knew Glen Gray they called it the Casa Loma Orchestra at the time. (?). Later they decided that they needed a name even though they were a co-operative for a long time. It was a very good band. Fletcher Henderson.....
